rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: # Immune system — innate and adaptive immunity ## 1. Introduction Opening frame for **Immune system — innate and adaptive immunity** — what the topic is, why it matters, a real-world hook (Nepal where possible), the map of what follows, and the learning outcomes (biology-plan.md §3.1, block I). Prose depth is written in the Human Health and Diseases fill pass. ## 2.…  ·  The immune system is the body's defence network, arranged in layers. **Innate immunity** is inborn, non-specific and immediate — barriers, phagocytes, inflammation. **Adaptive (acquired) immunity** is specific to each antigen, learns, remembers, and is carried by lymphocytes (B and T cells). Cell-mediated immunity (T cells) kills infected cells; humoral immunity (B cells → antibodies) neutralises free pathogens.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Trick 1: Innate (inborn, non-specific, 4 barriers: physical skin/mucus, physiological acid/tears, cellular WBC, cytokine) vs adaptive (acquired, specific, memory) — the two-column contrast is the whole answer.  ·  Trick 2: Cell-mediated (T cells, graft rejection) vs humoral (B cells → antibodies) — name the two arms of adaptive immunity.

Key terms and statements Every new term defined once; exam-grade definitions live here and in keyPoints (block VI).  ·  **Worked example.** A splinter enters the skin. Barriers fail (step 1). Neutrophils and macrophages arrive within hours; the area reddens and swells — inflammation (step 2). Macrophages present antigen to helper T cells, which activate B cells; antibodies appear after ~5–7 days (step 3).…  ·  ## 7. (3) Which cell does HIV attack and why does that collapse the whole adaptive response? (4) What is cell-mediated immunity — give one situation where it…  ·  ## 8. Summary and self-check 5–10 line chapter summary, self-check questions and the common-confusions list (block VIII) — completed in the unit fill pass.  ·  **Summary.** Defence is layered: instant barriers, fast non-specific innate cells, then specific adaptive humoral and cell-mediated arms that remember. Vaccination works because of that memory. **Self-check:** can you place neutrophil, B cell, helper T cell and NK cell in the right layer from memory?
